summary: Duplicate IAM principal aliasing prevents service-account impersonation across accounts
description: Several internal tools intermittently fail to assume or impersonate cross-account principals. Root cause appears to be 'principal aliasing' — when identity-mapping canonicalizes distinct principals to the same normalized identifier (duplicate role/service-account name across accounts/projects), the token exchange chooses the wrong identity and STS calls are rejected. This ticket tracks investigation and remediation for the normalization/lookup path in the identity mapper used by our dedicated provisioning and private deployment oncall flows.
impact: Oncall and ops-runner scripts intermittently fail to bootstrap in private and dedicated environments. Affected flows include: JIT debugging sessions, llm-health-check agent registration, and ephemeral debug-runner provisioning. Failures are intermittent (~2-4% of runs) but cause elevated debug-oncall latency and occasional failed deployments in eu-west and us-east regions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ops-runner to request ephemeral impersonation of service-account 'infra-runner' in project-a (GCP) or role 'infra-runner' in account-b (AWS).
2) Ensure a different project/account contains a principal with identical short name 'infra-runner' and overlapping identity-mapping rules (e.g., same tag/email alias).
3) Trigger the identity-mapper canonicalization path by requesting STS/OIDC exchange via the platform's provisioner.
4) Observe that the STS AssumeRole/ImpersonateServiceAccount call is directed to the wrong ARN/sa-email, resulting in AccessDenied or TokenExchangeFailure.
5) Re-run with unique principals (different short names) — issue does not reproduce.
logs: 2026-03-09T02:14:11Z provisioner: token-exchange failed: AccessDenied when calling AssumeRole for arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/infra-runner (expected 999999999), request-id=abc123
2026-03-09T02:14:11Z sts: AssumeRole called with audience 'redwood-provisioner' resolved principal arn mismatch
2026-03-09T02:14:09Z identity-mapper: normalized principal 'infra-runner' -> canonical_id 'infra-runner@canonical' (collision detected: sources=[project-a, project-b])
GCP Audit: 2026-03-09T02:14:10Z iam.serviceAccounts.actAs denied for serviceAccount:project-b@appspot.gserviceaccount.com (expected project-a service account).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: org-policy tag stripping caused lookup to drop account scope.

Reproduced locally by creating two principals with identical display names and running the identity-mapper binary with a debug trace. Mapper used short-name normalization rule before appending account/project, causing collisions.

Identity-mapper v1.17 uses an aggressive canonicalization pipeline: lowercasing + strip domain + collapse path segments. This allowed 'infra-runner' in multiple accounts to map to same key in cache/lookup table.
Cache layer amplification: when a colliding key is present, subsequent lookups returned the first-seen principal. This manifested as intermittent failures depending on insertion order and cache TTL.
AWS STS logs show the wrong ARN being supplied to AssumeRole; GCP impersonation attempted against a non-authorized service account (AccessDenied).
No evidence of credential compromise — authentication tokens themselves are valid, the problem is identity resolution in the platform's mapping service.
comments: Diego Morales (2026-03-10): Assigned; reproducer and unit test added to identity-mapper repo. Initial fix proposal: include account/project namespace in canonical key before normalization.
SRE Team (2026-03-11): Confirmed increased failure rate in eu-west between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-09 aligned with recent rollout of mapper v1.17.
Dev (2026-03-11): Quick mitigation deployed: disable short-name-only cache keys and add strict namespacing. Patch rolled to staging for smoke tests.
Security (2026-03-12): Reviewed logs for anomalous retries — no suspicious patterns; recommended monitoring dashboard for identity collisions.
resolution: Mitigation: rolled out identity-mapper patch (PR #487) that requires fully-qualified principal keys (account/project + principal) before any normalization, plus a cache migration to evict old short-name entries. Full fix: added unit and e2e tests, and a feature-flagged rollout to prod. Rollout schedule: gradual 10->50->100% over 24h with guard rails and canary on dedicated infra. Monitoring: new Grafana panel for collision-rate and STS AccessDenied trends. Follow-up: implement collision alerting and add chaos tests for canonicalization edge cases.
next_steps: 1) Finish canary rollout and monitor collision-rate metrics for 48h.
2) Backfill and invalidate short-name cache entries in prod within maintenance window.
3) Add identity collision alert (pager) for >0.1% collision rate over 10m.
4) Document canonicalization rules in onboarding docs for infra teams.
5) Run cross-account fuzz tests in CI to detect future regressions.
